meta: How does a self-driving car see a person walking in the dark? The answer is LiDAR, a technology that measures distance with light. Explained simply in about a minute.

muc.title: How does LiDAR work?
muc.text: In the dark of night, a self-driving car can still clearly see a person walking ahead. The secret is a technology called LiDAR.

muc.title: Measuring distance with light
muc.text: LiDAR means measuring distance with light. It's like a bat listening for echoes, but it uses laser pulses instead of sound.

muc.title: Send a laser flash
muc.text: Step one: the device sends out a very short laser flash that your eyes can't see. The flash flies out, hits an object and bounces back.

muc.title: Time the trip there and back
muc.text: Step two: the device times how long it takes, from sending to receiving. Light is so fast that going 15 meters and back takes only one ten-millionth of a second.

muc.title: Work out the distance
muc.text: Step three: work out the distance. Multiply the time by the speed of light, then divide by two, because the light went there and came back.

muc.title: Millions of dots
muc.text: The device does this hundreds of thousands of times per second, in every direction. Each measurement is one dot. Together they make a 3D map called a point cloud.

muc.title: AI reads the point cloud
muc.text: Then AI reads those dots to tell what is a person, what is a car, and how far away they are. That's how the car knows when to brake.

muc.title: LiDAR is all around you
muc.text: LiDAR is also in robot vacuums, mapping drones and the Pro iPhones.

muc.title: Measure height with your phone
muc.text: Want to try it? Open the Measure app on a Pro iPhone and point it at a person. It will show their height on its own.
